title: You're still you
hook: Islam is a faith, not a costume. You don't have to become someone else.

screens.text: Since your shahada, people may have offered you a new name, new clothes, new food, maybe a whole new accent. Kindly meant, mostly. But here's the truth: **Islam asks you to change some things, not to become someone else.**

**Islam is for every people.** The Qur'an says Allah made humanity into peoples and tribes *so that you may know one another*, and that the most honored in His sight is the most mindful of Him [Q 49:13].
bubbles: Not the most Arab, not the most South Asian.
Black, Latino, white, Asian, Native: there are Muslims from every one of these backgrounds.

Not quite. Honor with Allah comes from being mindful of Him, not from a language.
Not quite. Honor with Allah comes from being mindful of Him, not from how you look.

screens.text: **Two kinds of things.** **Islam** is what comes from the Qur'an and the Prophet's teaching ﷺ: praying, honesty, modesty, no pork or alcohol. **Culture** is how a particular people live: their food, clothes, wedding customs, languages.
bubbles: Muslims from Senegal, Indonesia and Texas live Islam with different cultures, and all of it is fine where it doesn't clash with Islam [Field Guide ch. 2].

items.text: Muslim men wear a long robe (thobe)
items.why: Islam asks for modest, clean clothes. A thobe is one style; jeans and a loose shirt work too.

items.text: You must eat with your hands, sitting on the floor
items.why: Eating with your right hand is the sunnah; plates, forks and tables are fine.
It's in the Qur'an. You'll learn the food basics on Day 13.
What modest looks like can vary from place to place, within its limits (Day 38).

items.text: You have to speak Arabic or Urdu at the masjid
items.why: Arabic is for the prayer and the Qur'an. Everything else can be in your own language.

items.text: Your family's recipes are off-limits now
items.why: Not true, and not Islam. Keep them: just swap out pork and alcohol for halal options.

screens.text: **Your name.** You don't have to change it. A name only needs changing if its meaning goes against Islam, like worship of someone other than Allah, or a clearly bad meaning [IslamOnline (Siddiqi); IslamWeb 393040].
bubbles: Most names are fine. **Keep your family name.** It honors the parents who gave it to you.

screens.prompt: At the masjid, an uncle tells Destiny, "Now you need a Muslim name!" What's true?

options.text: Destiny can keep her name; it has a fine meaning
options.feedback: Right. Only a name with a meaning against Islam needs changing. Many converts keep theirs.

options.text: Every convert has to take an Arabic name
options.feedback: Not quite. That's a cultural habit, not a rule. Most names are fine as they are.

options.text: She can keep it, but must drop her family name
options.feedback: Not quite. Islam values keeping your family name, out of respect for your parents.

screens.text: **How to tell the difference.** When someone says "Muslims must do X," it's fine to ask, kindly: *"Is that from the Qur'an or the Sunnah, or is it a custom?"* [Welcome to Islam D5] Then check with {{mentor.name}} or your imam.
bubbles: Many converts say the hardest part wasn't Islam: it was being handed someone else's culture along with it [Yaqeen 2025].

screens.situation: Chris, a Black convert from Atlanta, keeps hearing at the masjid that his music, his clothes and even his slang aren't "Islamic." He's starting to feel he doesn't belong.

options.text: Sort it out: ask which ones come from Islam, and check them with his imam
options.feedback: Yes. Some may be real points, many will be custom. Asking calmly sorts out which is which.

options.text: Change everything so people stop commenting
options.feedback: Understandable, but erasing yourself leads to burnout. Islam asks you to grow, not disappear.
Please don't. Find the kind people there, and talk to the imam. You belong as much as anyone.

screens.optional_extra: Next time someone tells you "Muslims must…," try asking: "Is that Islam or culture?"

screens.text: Islam changes what's against it, not who you are. Keep your name, your family and your culture where they fit.
You're not a copy of anyone. You're you, now Muslim.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah made peoples and tribes to know one another; the most honored is the most mindful of Him [Q 49:13].
- Culture has a real place where it doesn't conflict with Islam; no culture fully represents Islam [Field Guide ch. 2].
- A name needs changing only if its meaning conflicts with Islam (e.g., "servant of" someone other than Allah) or is clearly bad; family names are kept [IslamOnline, Siddiqi; IslamWeb 393040; Field Guide ch. 3].
- Asking for the basis of a "rule" and checking with a qualified teacher is sound advice [Welcome to Islam D5].
- Converts report pressure to adopt others' cultures as a major pain point; ~50% of US converts are Black and 17% Hispanic [Yaqeen 2025; Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices, themes 2 and 11].

**Likely questions**
- *"Convert or revert?"* Either is fine; some prefer "revert" because of the idea of fitra (natural faith). Their choice.
- *"Do I need Arabic?"* Only the prayer's words and Qur'an you recite, learned bit by bit. Du'a and daily life in any language.
- *"My name is Christian / a saint's name."* Don't rule; most scholars allow keeping names without a bad meaning; send specifics to the imam.
- *"Birthdays?"* Scholars differ; don't rule; ask the imam.
- *"People at the masjid keep correcting me."* Validate; suggest the mentor; the ones who correct harshly don't represent Islam.

**Escalate:** specific name rulings; holiday and birthday questions (Q5); anyone feeling unwelcome because of race (flag to the imam with consent).

**Don't:** endorse or mock any ethnic culture; tell them to change clothes, name or speech; claim every custom they meet is wrong.
